title: 拉瓦锡发表《化学基础论》

video.title: 安托万·拉瓦锡：现代化学之父
video.title_en: Antoine Lavoisier: The Father of Modern Chemistry

summary.text: 1789年，在法国大革命爆发的同年，安托万·拉瓦锡（Antoine Lavoisier）出版了划时代的巨著《化学基础论》（Traité Élémentaire de Chimie）。这本书被认为是历史上第一部现代化学教科书。书中，拉瓦锡彻底抛弃了古老的“四元素说”和“燃素说”，给出了“元素”的现代定义：无法通过化学手段进一步分解的物质。他列出了历史上第一张包含33种化学元素的清单（虽然其中包含了光和热，以及一些后来被证明是化合物的物质如石灰），并建立了一套全新的、逻辑严密的化学命名法（如硫酸、氧化物等），这套命名规则至今仍在使用。
summary.text_en: In 1789, the same year the French Revolution began, Antoine Lavoisier published his monumental work 'Elementary Treatise on Chemistry' (Traité Élémentaire de Chimie). This book is considered the first modern chemistry textbook in history. In it, Lavoisier completely discarded the ancient 'Four Elements' theory and the 'Phlogiston' theory, offering the modern definition of an 'element': a substance that cannot be broken down further by chemical means. He listed the first table of 33 chemical elements (though it included light and caloric, and some substances later proven to be compounds like lime), and established a brand new, logical system of chemical nomenclature (like sulfuric acid, oxides, etc.), which is still in use today.
key_points: 出版了第一部现代化学教科书
给出了“元素”的现代操作性定义
列出了第一张包含33种元素的列表
建立了现代化学命名法体系
彻底推翻了统治化学百年的“燃素说”
key_points_en: Published the first modern chemistry textbook
Provided the modern operational definition of an 'element'
Listed the first table containing 33 elements
Established the system of modern chemical nomenclature
Completely overthrew the 'Phlogiston Theory' that ruled chemistry for a century

story.text: 拉瓦锡不仅是一位天才的科学家，还是一位一丝不苟的会计师（他是税务官）。他把这种通过天平称量的精确精神带入了化学。他曾自豪地说：“我在化学中引发了一场革命。”在这本书中，他不仅重新定义了元素，还展示了如何通过简单的逻辑（而不是神秘的炼金术符号）来理解化学反应。他把化学从混乱的“菜谱”变成了严谨的科学。然而，他的税务官身份最终害了他。在法国大革命的恐怖时期，他被送上了断头台。数学家拉格朗日悲叹道：“砍下这颗头颅只需一瞬间，但也许一百年也长不出这样一颗脑袋了。”
story.text_en: Lavoisier was not only a brilliant scientist but also a meticulous accountant (he was a tax collector). He brought this spirit of precision via the balance scale into chemistry. He once proudly declared, 'I have induced a revolution in chemistry.' In this book, he not only redefined elements but showed how to understand chemical reactions through simple logic (rather than mystical alchemical symbols). He turned chemistry from a chaotic 'cookbook' into a rigorous science. However, his role as a tax collector eventually doomed him. During the Reign of Terror in the French Revolution, he was sent to the guillotine. The mathematician Lagrange lamented, 'It took them only an instant to cut off this head, and one hundred years might not suffice to reproduce its like.'

fun_facts.text: 这本书中精美的仪器插图（如气量计）其实是由拉瓦锡的妻子玛丽-安妮（Marie-Anne）绘制的。她不仅是他的插画师，还是他的翻译和实验助手，是“现代化学之母”。
fun_facts.text_en: The exquisite illustrations of instruments (like the gasometer) in this book were actually drawn by Lavoisier's wife, Marie-Anne. She was not only his illustrator but also his translator and lab assistant, effectively the 'Mother of Modern Chemistry'.

fun_facts.text: 尽管拉瓦锡极具革命性，但他还是在元素列表中保留了两个“幽灵”：光（Light）和热质（Caloric）。他认为热是一种无重量的流体。
fun_facts.text_en: Despite being revolutionary, Lavoisier kept two 'ghosts' in his list of elements: Light and Caloric. He believed heat was a weightless fluid.

fun_facts.text: 拉瓦锡也是“质量守恒定律”的奠基人。他在书中写道：“在任何化学反应中，物质的总量既不增加也不减少。”
fun_facts.text_en: Lavoisier was also the founder of the 'Law of Conservation of Mass'. He wrote in the book: 'In any chemical reaction, the total quantity of matter neither increases nor decreases.'

simple_explanation.text:
在拉瓦锡之前，化学就像一本用密码写成的巫师笔记，每个人用的符号都不一样，理论也是乱七八糟（比如认为东西燃烧是因为里面有‘燃素’）。
拉瓦锡写了一本“字典”和“语法书”。
1. 字典：他列出了什么是真正的“积木”（元素），比如氧、氢、硫、铁。
2. 语法：他规定了怎么给化合物起名（比如“硫”和“氧”结合叫“硫酸”）。
这就好比秦始皇统一度量衡和文字，从此以后，全世界的化学家终于可以说同一种语言了。
simple_explanation.text_en:
Before Lavoisier, chemistry was like a wizard's notebook written in code; everyone used different symbols, and theories were messy (like believing things burned because they contained 'phlogiston').
Lavoisier wrote a 'Dictionary' and a 'Grammar Book'.
1. Dictionary: He listed what the real 'building blocks' (elements) were, like Oxygen, Hydrogen, Sulfur, Iron.
2. Grammar: He set rules for naming compounds (e.g., 'Sulfur' combined with 'Oxygen' is called 'Sulfuric Acid').
It was like the First Emperor of China unifying weights, measures, and writing; from then on, chemists worldwide could finally speak the same language.

applications.title: 化学交流
applications.text: 直到今天，我们使用的化学命名法（如二氧化碳、氯化钠）依然遵循拉瓦锡在1789年制定的基本规则。
applications.text_en: To this day, the chemical nomenclature we use (like carbon dioxide, sodium chloride) still follows the basic rules established by Lavoisier in 1789.

applications.title: 科学教育
applications.text: 《化学基础论》确立了教科书的范式：从简单的定义出发，通过实验推导结论，而不是罗列杂乱的观察。
applications.text_en: 'Elementary Treatise on Chemistry' established the paradigm for textbooks: starting from simple definitions and deriving conclusions through experiment, rather than listing chaotic observations.

impact.text: 这本书的出版标志着化学作为一门现代科学的正式诞生。它终结了长达千年的炼金术时代，确立了“元素”作为化学核心概念的地位。拉瓦锡整理的元素列表虽然包含了一些错误（如把石灰和镁土当成元素，把光和热当成元素），但它为后来的道尔顿原子论和门捷列夫元素周期表搭建了坚实的舞台。正如他所说，这是一场“化学革命”。
impact.text_en: The publication of this book marked the formal birth of chemistry as a modern science. It ended the millennial era of alchemy and established the 'element' as the core concept of chemistry. Although Lavoisier's list contained some errors (treating lime and magnesia as elements, and including light and caloric), it set the stage for Dalton's atomic theory and Mendeleev's periodic table. As he said, it was a 'Chemical Revolution'.

influenced_by.contribution: 波义耳（拉瓦锡直接采纳了波义耳关于“元素是不可分解物质”的定义，并将其付诸实践）
influenced_by.contribution_en: Robert Boyle (Lavoisier directly adopted Boyle's definition of an element as an 'undecomposable substance' and put it into practice)

influenced_by.contribution: 普利斯特里（提供了关键的氧气发现，虽然普利斯特里解释错了，但拉瓦锡利用它建立了正确的燃烧理论）
influenced_by.contribution_en: Joseph Priestley (Provided the key discovery of oxygen; although Priestley explained it wrongly, Lavoisier used it to build the correct combustion theory)

influenced.contribution: 道尔顿（在拉瓦锡元素定义和质量守恒的基础上，提出了原子论，认为每种元素对应一种原子）
influenced.contribution_en: John Dalton (Building on Lavoisier's definition of elements and conservation of mass, proposed Atomic Theory, assigning atoms to each element)

influenced.contribution: 贝采利乌斯（继承并发展了拉瓦锡的命名法，引入了现代的字母符号系统，如H, O, Fe）
influenced.contribution_en: Jöns Jacob Berzelius (Inherited and developed Lavoisier's nomenclature, introducing the modern letter symbol system like H, O, Fe)

influence_chain.legacy_text: 在法国大革命的战火中，他为化学世界建立了一套新秩序。
influence_chain.legacy_text_en: Amidst the flames of the French Revolution, he established a new order for the chemical world.

quiz.question: 拉瓦锡在《化学基础论》中对“元素”给出的定义是什么？
quiz.question_en: What definition did Lavoisier give for an 'element' in his 'Elementary Treatise on Chemistry'?
options: 构成万物的四种基本性质：冷、热、干、湿
任何我们目前无法通过化学手段进一步分解的物质
由原子组成的微小颗粒
options_en: The four basic qualities: hot, cold, dry, wet
Any substance that we cannot currently break down further by chemical means
quiz.explanation: 这是一个操作性的定义。拉瓦锡承认，有些被他列为元素的物质（如石灰）未来可能会被证明是化合物，但在当时的技术下它们无法被分解，所以暂时视为元素。
quiz.explanation_en: This was an operational definition. Lavoisier admitted that some substances he listed as elements (like lime) might be proven to be compounds in the future, but since they couldn't be decomposed with current technology, they were treated as elements.
